name: Architectural Promenade — Temporal Composition of Multi-Modal Prediction Error
short_description: Spatial sequence produces emotional trajectory through thresholds; compression-release, gradual revelation, spatial rhythm, and climactic revelation as compositional techniques
structural_pattern: The architectural promenade is the deliberate design of spatial sequence to produce a specific emotional trajectory over time. As the visitor moves through the building, they encounter THRESHOLDS — transitions between zones that differ in spatial volume, light, material, acoustics, temperature, and view. Each threshold is a multi-modal PE event. The sequence of thresholds is the temporal structure — the 'score' the architect composes. Key techniques include: COMPRESSION-RELEASE (narrow/low/dark → tall/wide/bright, building prediction and violating maximally); GRADUAL REVELATION (curved path progressively revealing space); SPATIAL RHYTHM (alternation of spatial types); CLIMACTIC REVELATION (escalating PE events building to maximum — the awe trigger).
higher_order_principle: The architecture-as-composition thesis formalized. As music orchestrates auditory PE over time (BRECVEMA), architecture orchestrates multi-modal PE over space-time. The visitor's movement through the building IS the temporal dimension. The architect is a composer whose medium is the PE trajectory through spatial sequence.

compositional_techniques.compression_release: Constricted space → expansive space; PE scales with contrast (Optimal ratio 1:3 to 1:8)
compositional_techniques.gradual_revelation: Curved path progressively revealing space, distributing PE over time
compositional_techniques.climactic_revelation: Escalating PE events building to maximum (Bernini approach to St. Peter's)

threshold_pe_density_goldilocks.too_few: Low PE density (> 60s interval) → monotony, habituation, disengagement
threshold_pe_density_goldilocks.optimal: Moderate threshold density (20-45s interval) → sustained engagement, maintained GSR responsivity
threshold_pe_density_goldilocks.too_many: High PE density (< 15s interval) → fatigue, tonic GSR elevation, overstimulation

causal_links.evidence_base: PE at threshold scales with contrast between preceding and succeeding zones across ALL modalities. Ellard: GSR response at spatial transitions scales with spatial contrast magnitude.
Low PE → smooth transition. Moderate PE → interest, spatial delight. High PE (with vastness, at climax) → awe (AX3). Context (agency, purpose) determines valence.
Many thresholds in rapid succession → potential overstimulation. Few thresholds over long path → monotony. Optimal density = temporal Goldilocks zone.
Thresholds where MULTIPLE modalities change simultaneously produce stronger emotional responses. Therme Vals steam room entry is a five-modality threshold.

scope_conditions: Applies to buildings designed for sequential experience — museums, sacred buildings, memorials, hospitality
Less applicable to random-access buildings (open-plan offices, malls) though these contain unavoidable sequential transitions
The 'score' is composed by architect but 'performed' by visitor — deviations create different PE trajectories
Speed of movement modulates temporal distribution
First visit vs. repeat: promenade is most powerful on first experience
moderators: Visitor pace: faster movement compresses sequence, potentially exceeding optimal PE density
Group vs. solo: social interaction diverts attention from spatial PE
Familiarity: repeated visits reduce PE but may increase appreciation of compositional structure
Cognitive engagement: distracted visitors miss threshold PE events

interactions.nature: Light changes at thresholds are primary contributor. L1 provides luminance PE at each transition; SC3 provides temporal sequence.
Material changes at thresholds contribute to cross-modal PE.
Acoustic changes at thresholds (different reverberation) contribute to threshold PE.
Climactic revelation is trigger for AX3 awe. SC3 describes how preceding sequence amplifies the awe.
Each threshold is an AX6 multi-modal PE event. SC3 orchestrates these events over time.
